title: Hit-and-run driver sought after group of bicyclists reportedly struck in Montclair
text:
2 dead after suspected DUI driver strikes group of bicyclists, drags victim for a mile in Montclair hit-and-run, witnesses say - ABC7 Los Angeles 
 24/7 Live Los Angeles Orange County Inland Empire Ventura County California 2 killed after driver strikes group of bicyclists, drags victim for a mile in Montclair: Witnesses 
 Police in Montclair are searching for a hit-and-run driver following reports that a group of bicyclists were struck by a vehicle overnight. KABC By Madison Weil , Tim Pulliam Monday, October 26, 2026 4:25AM Share Follow ABC7 on Google MONTCLAIR, Calif. (KABC) -- Two people are dead after a suspected drunk driver struck a group of bicyclists in Montclair and then took off, police confirmed.
 The incident unfolded just before 11 p.m. Saturday at the intersection of Kingsley Street and Tudor Avenue, according to the Montclair Police Department.
 About 30 people were riding bicycles when a suspected drunk driver struck several of the riders and took off. Witnesses say the group was participating in a self-coordinated Halloween ride.
 The driver kept going after hitting the bicyclists, dragging the second victim for at least a mile, according to witnesses. The suspect then ditched his blood-stained car and ran away.
 One bicyclist died at the scene. Two others were taken to the hospital, where one of them later succumbed to her injuries, police said. The other rider suffered major injuries but is in stable condition.
 Just hours after the deadly collision, police found the driver at his home near the scene. Valentin Alberto Rodriguez, 38, was arrested on suspicion of several charges, including driving under the influence.
 Rodriguez now faces several felonies, including hit-and-run and gross vehicular manslaughter while intoxicated.
 Winni Mercado lives nearby and said she heard the aftermath of the crash; loved ones crying and wailing over a victim's body on the pavement.
 "It was just awful. It was just awful. I know that I will never get that sound out of my head. Just feeling that pain," she said.

 Neighbors and loved ones are left grieving.
 "My heart breaks for you. I can't fathom or imagine what they're going through right now...on something that was so innocent. Just kids having fun. My prayers are with them," Mercado said.
 Anyone with further information about the collision is urged to contact the Montclair Police Department at (909) 21-4771.
